hypothesis: Four bounded workers reduce evaluation wall time relative to one worker without changing candidate outcomes or weakening provenance validation.
candidate_selection: Pinned baseline and known fixed revision for each task, two identical repetitions per revision, eight jobs per campaign. No agent-generated patches.
primary_metric: Median of five paired serial wall seconds divided by parallel wall seconds; time includes input verification, grader execution, bounded capture, atomic records and journal, but excludes initial source fetch and protocol snapshots.
quantile_rule: Nearest rank on sorted values, ceil(p*n)-1.
acceptance: All 80 results match pinned base rejection/fixed acceptance, and every campaign passes bundle audit. Report measured speedup even if <=1. No reruns to optimize headline.
abort: Stop the scheduling measurement at the first unexpected outcome or audit error; retain artifacts and failure record. Any repaired protocol gets a new version.
claim_limit: Local CPU evaluation orchestration on two small historical graders and synthetic faults. No distributed fleet, inference serving, hostile-code sandbox, agent task solving, or learning claim. Baseline is the same runner with one worker.
